skill.name: daily-dev
skill.description: Use daily.dev APIs to find current developer articles, feeds, tags, bookmarks, and profile data for AI-assisted research workflows.
skill.summary: Connect AI assistants to current daily.dev developer content and personalized feeds.
skill.author: dailydotdev

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, inline code, or legitimate daily.dev API references. Real concerns remain around automatic credential retrieval from OS secret stores, persistent shell profile token loading, and the executable !`curl ... | jq` substitution that performs live shell and network access.

remediation.issue: Executable markdown command substitution fetches the OpenAPI spec during skill processing.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the !`curl ... | jq` block with static endpoint documentation or instruct the agent to fetch the spec only after explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to retrieve API tokens from OS credential storage before asking the user.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before reading secure storage, and keep token values out of logs, summaries, and generated files.

remediation.issue: Setup examples recommend auto-loading the token from hidden shell profile files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer temporary environment variables or documented secret managers, and warn users about persistent shell profile changes.

content.user_title: Research Current Developer Trends with daily.dev
content.value_statement: LLMs can miss recent developer news because their training data becomes stale. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows to daily.dev feeds, tags, posts, and bookmarks.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to authenticate with the daily.dev public API using a user API token.
Documents daily.dev feed, tag, post, bookmark, search, and profile workflows.
Helps create personalized feeds based on a developer stack or project topic.
Supports research workflows that compare posts, sources, tags, and discussions.
Describes rate limits, common API errors, and token handling practices.
limitations: Requires a daily.dev Plus subscription and a valid API token.
Depends on live daily.dev API availability and rate limits.
Does not verify the quality of every third-party article returned by daily.dev.
May require user approval before running shell commands or reading stored credentials.

use_cases.title: Build a stack-specific reading feed
use_cases.description: Create a daily.dev feed that follows the technologies used in a project or GitHub portfolio.

use_cases.title: Prepare a current technical briefing
use_cases.description: Collect popular and discussed posts for a weekly summary with links to current sources.

use_cases.title: Research a new technology area
use_cases.description: Find sources, tags, posts, and bookmark lists for a focused learning workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Find current articles
prompt_templates.prompt: Use daily.dev to find recent articles about React performance. Summarize the top themes and include source links.

prompt_templates.title: Create a project feed
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project stack and suggest daily.dev tags for a custom feed. Ask before changing my profile or follows.

prompt_templates.title: Compare community perspectives
prompt_templates.prompt: Search daily.dev for recent posts about Kubernetes cost optimization. Compare where sources agree and disagree.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an ongoing research workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a weekly daily.dev research workflow for my backend team. Include feeds, bookmarks, rate limit handling, and approval steps.

output_examples.input: What is trending in TypeScript this week?
output: A short trend summary grouped by themes.
Links to daily.dev posts and sources.
Suggested tags to follow for future updates.

output_examples.input: Help me learn the stack for this repository.
output: A proposed custom feed and bookmark list plan.

output_examples.input: Compare recent opinions about serverless databases.

best_practices: Ask for user approval before reading stored API tokens or changing profile data.
Use focused tags and source filters to reduce irrelevant results.
Respect daily.dev rate limits and retry only after the documented reset time.
anti_patterns: Do not paste daily.dev API tokens into prompts, code, logs, or summaries.
Do not follow tags, update profiles, or create bookmarks without user approval.
Do not treat community popularity as proof that an article is technically correct.

faq.question: Do I need a daily.dev account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires a daily.dev Plus subscription and an API token for authenticated requests.

faq.question: Can it use Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it send my token to third-party sites?
faq.answer: The skill warns that tokens should only be sent to api.daily.dev. Users should still review commands before execution.

faq.question: Can it create feeds and bookmarks?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes API workflows for custom feeds, bookmark lists, and saved posts.

faq.question: Is the content always accurate?
faq.answer: No. daily.dev aggregates community content, so important claims should be checked against primary sources.

faq.question: What should I approve manually?
faq.answer: Approve credential access, profile updates, follows, bookmark changes, and any shell command that contacts the network.
